belief: My loved one in heaven is watching me and is disappointed in me.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that a loved one in heaven is watching you and is disappointed in you, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Guilt about things left unsaid or undone before your loved one died. A parent or grandparent who was often critical while alive. Sayings like “Your mother is looking down on you.” Grief mixed with regret. Feeling that you are not living up to a loved one’s hopes.
teaches: Scripture does not teach that our loved ones in heaven monitor our daily lives. It does teach that in God’s presence there will be no more crying, mourning, or pain. Those who die in Christ are with the Lord, made whole, and filled with joy. In heaven, there is joy over every sinner who repents, not disappointment. Whatever your loved one felt on earth, in heaven they share God’s perfect love and freedom from sorrow.
self_statements: Mom is watching me and shaking her head.
Dad would be so disappointed in me.
I let them down, and now they know everything.
They’re upset I didn’t visit more.
I have to live up to what they wanted.
They see every mistake I make.
errors: Assuming you know what your loved one in heaven thinks.
Picturing them with the same criticism they may have had on earth.
Letting regret shape your picture of heaven.
Overlooking that heaven has no sorrow or disappointment.
questions: Does Scripture say my loved one is watching my daily life?
Is there sorrow or disappointment in heaven, according to Revelation 21:4?
What is heaven filled with, according to Psalm 16:11?
Am I picturing them as they were at their worst on earth?
If they are with Christ, what would they want for me now?
Is this guilt from God or from regret?
What regret could I bring to God instead?
truth: My loved one in heaven is not disappointed in me. In God’s presence there is no more sorrow, mourning, or pain, only joy. Those who are with Christ share His perfect love. I can bring my regrets to God, receive His forgiveness, and honor my loved one by living well.

log: Each day, write one regret and then: “God forgives me, and my loved one is at peace.”

prayer: Father, thank You that in Your presence there is no sorrow, only joy. Help me reject the lie that my loved one in heaven is disappointed in me. I bring You my regrets and receive Your forgiveness. Help me honor my loved one by living in Your grace. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
